name: Tacit
headline: Two faces of one program
standfirst: An experimental language gives AI authors a compact notation and human reviewers an expanded view of the same program.
evidence: Toolglass reviewed the public project documentation. Maintainer claims were not independently reproduced.

body.heading: What it is
paragraphs: Tacit is an experimental AI-first programming language with an LLVM compilation route. Its author treats the abstract syntax tree, rather than a human-readable text file, as the authoritative program.

body.heading: The idea worth stealing
paragraphs: The project describes two lossless presentations: a dense view for model generation and a more expansive view for human inspection. It is a serious design question hiding inside an easy-to-dismiss slogan. If software is increasingly authored by a machine but owned by a human, why must both parties read the same surface syntax? The essential word is lossless. A pretty human explanation that cannot reconstruct the exact machine program is a commentary, not an alternate representation.

body.heading: Why now
paragraphs: AI-generated changes have made provenance, inspectability and exact edit boundaries urgent. This is not proof that a model-oriented language produces better code; it is an architectural hypothesis about how to separate writing from review.

body.heading: Maturity and limits
paragraphs: The repository claims a Phase 6 Tacit-Lite toolchain that parses, typechecks, inspects, compiles and executes a frozen subset. The claims are maintainer-reported. Its ecosystem, toolchain trust, actual token efficiency and long-term language stability need independent tests. The idea predates Tacit in projectional editing, structured editors and intentional programming; its interest lies in the new AI audience.

verdict: A testable experiment in separating authoring from review.
nextStep: Round-trip 20 programs through dense and inspection views, including malformed code and refactors; compare AST hashes and diagnostic precision.
